title: Transcript of Chair Powell's Press Conference -- September 17, 2025
summary: The FOMC cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-4.25% on September 17, 2025, citing a shift in the balance of risks with downside risks to employment having risen. Chair Powell noted that while the unemployment rate remains low at 4.3%, payroll job gains have slowed significantly to 29,000 per month, and total PCE inflation rose 2.7% year-over-year with core PCE at 2.9%. The committee continues to reduce its balance sheet and raised near-term inflation expectations citing tariff effects. [Note: This summary accurately reflects the transcript content, but the source is a press conference transcript, not a formal FOMC statement.]
key_points: FOMC voted to lower target range for federal funds rate by 25 bps to 4-4.25 percent
Payroll job gains slowed to just 29,000 per month over the past three months, below the breakeven rate needed to hold unemployment constant
Unemployment rate edged up to 4.3% in August; median SEP projects 4.5% at end of 2025
Total PCE inflation was 2.7% and core PCE was 2.9% over 12 months ending August, higher than earlier in the year
Median SEP projection: federal funds rate at 3.6% end of 2025, 3.4% end of 2026, 3.1% end of 2027 (down 25 bps from June projections)
Committee raised near-term inflation expectations due to tariff news, but longer-term expectations remain anchored near 2%
Powell stated risks to inflation are tilted to the upside and risks to employment to the downside in the near term
why_it_matters: This press conference reveals the Fed's increasing concern about labor market softening while navigating resurgent inflation pressures from tariffs. The 25 bps cut signals the Fed is prioritizing employment risks, but the elevated inflation readings and upward-trending near-term expectations suggest a cautious, data-dependent approach going forward. Market participants should note the revised dot plot path is lower than June, indicating accommodation is expected to continue if employment continues to cool.
macro_context: The Fed is managing a delicate balancing act: unemployment has ticked up, job creation has slowed dramatically, and tariff-driven goods inflation is pushing headline and core PCE above earlier-year readings. The dual mandate is now in tension, with near-term employment risks elevated while inflation risks remain tilted to the upside. The Fed's base case treats tariff effects as a one-time price level shift, but Powell explicitly acknowledged the risk that inflationary effects could be more persistent.
market_structure_context: The committee continues reducing its securities holdings, maintaining the quantitative tightening process while cutting rates. No changes to the operating framework or monetary policy tools were discussed.
